assumptions: The NL states that there are twelve finite states but does not provide exact state names or the full original transition table; the twelve state names and several capacity partition conditions are inferred from the described dispatch cases.

The model is represented as a guard-driven condition-classification FSM using forced transitions from any current state, because the NL says states are selected by logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC rather than by named external events.
SoC suitability for battery discharge is modeled with an assumed threshold SoC >= 0.3; the NL specifies the 0.95 full-charge threshold but not the low/discharge suitability threshold.
Pd2max and Pbatt_dis_max/Pbatt_ch_max are introduced as capacity variables to express DG2 and battery limits mentioned in the NL, but their exact original identifiers were not supplied.

Load cut-out is asserted only in the illegal overload state to satisfy the NL obligation that load cut-in/cut-out commands exist; the NL does not provide detailed load-shedding logic for normal states.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, EMS handles RES production according to SoC thresholds; zero production is modeled as idle.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, EMS serves all demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL and SoC is at least 0.95, residual renewable power is spare.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch uses RES first and batteries when SoC is suitable.
Dispatch priority uses LNG before diesel units when renewable power is below load demand.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: with zero load and no renewable production, the initial dispatch should land in ZeroIdle with no generation, battery power, spare power, or load shedding.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_idle

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: with PL=0, positive RES, and SoC below 0.95, renewable production should be sent to battery charging.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_charges_battery_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: with PL=0, positive RES, and SoC exactly 0.95, renewable production should become spare power rather than charging.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES covers positive load and SoC is below 0.95, all load should be served from RES and residual RES should charge batteries.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_charges_battery_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: when RES covers positive load and SoC is exactly 0.95, residual RES should be spare power rather than battery charge.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: with RES below load, SoC exactly 0.3, and deficit equal to battery discharge capacity, batteries should cover the deficit before LNG or DGs.
scenario_results.name: battery_assist_at_soc_and_discharge_capacity_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: when RES and battery are insufficient but deficit is exactly within LNG capacity, LNG alone should be cut in with requested generator power equal to the deficit.
scenario_results.name: lng_only_after_battery_capacity_exceeded

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC probe: when SoC is below 0.3 and LNG can cover deficit plus Pgmax/5 charging margin, LNG should both serve load and charge the battery.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: with suitable SoC and deficit above LNG capacity but within LNG plus DG1, LNG and DG1 should be cut in while DG2 remains out.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_normal_after_lng_capacity_exceeded

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC probe: when LNG alone cannot cover the low-SoC charging case, DG1 should be added and Pd1max/10 should be requested for battery charging.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_dg1_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES, battery, LNG, and DG1 are insufficient but deficit is within LNG+DG1+DG2, DG2 should be cut in as the last priority.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_dg2_last_priority

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start overload probe: when extreme demand exceeds all RES and thermal resources, the illegal overload completion state should activate all thermal units, cover the remaining lack by battery discharge, and shed load.
scenario_results.name: illegal_overload_all_thermal_and_battery_lack

evidence: DSL uses SoC >= 0.3 / SoC < 0.3 for battery suitability, while GroundingMap assumptions state: "SoC suitability for battery discharge is modeled with an assumed threshold SoC >= 0.3; the NL specifies the 0.95 full-charge threshold but not the low/discharge suitability threshold."

DSL sets cmd_load_cut_out = 1 in IllegalOverloadAllThermalBattery, while the NL says the overload state activates all thermal units and covers the lack by battery discharge; detailed load-shedding logic is not provided.
GroundingMap assumptions state: "Load cut-out is asserted only in the illegal overload state ... the NL does not provide detailed load-shedding logic for normal states."
findings.summary: The model is broadly faithful to the described 12-state dispatch logic, but several important thresholds and overload/load-shedding details are inferred rather than directly stated in the NL.

evidence: DSL declares Pbatt_ch_max but no transition guard or action caps Pbatt_charge by Pbatt_ch_max.
Design diagnostics report W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for Pbatt_ch_max and W_VARIABLE_DECLARED_NEVER_USED for Pbatt_ch_max.
Input five_component_summary is {}.
findings.summary: Most major EMS components are represented, but battery charge capacity is declared without being used to constrain charging outputs, and the five-component summary is empty.

evidence: IllegalOverloadAllThermalBattery assigns Pbatt_discharge = PL - Ppv - Pw - eng3_Pmax - Pd1max - Pd2max without checking Pbatt_dis_max.
RESCharge and ZeroLoadCharge assign Pbatt_charge from surplus renewable power without checking Pbatt_ch_max.
The NL says EMS issues cut-in and cut-out commands for generating units and loads, but the model only toggles load cut-out in the illegal overload state.
findings.summary: The model covers the stated dispatch cases, but it does not fully cover unspecified-but-relevant boundary behavior for battery charge limits, battery discharge limits in overload, or detailed load cut-in/cut-out policy.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary metrics show n_events = 0.
DSL uses global forced transitions ! * -> state for all dispatch classifications.
NL mentions changing time periods and operating conditions; the DSL models only instantaneous conditions over current variable values.
findings.summary: The EMS is modeled as an instantaneous guard-classification FSM with no events, no temporal dwell behavior, and no explicit engine ramping or persistence beyond current state labels.

evidence: DSL transition: ! * -> IllegalOverloadAllThermalBattery : if [PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw < PL && PL - Ppv - Pw > eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max].
NL: "The overload completion state is illegal ... and the state shall never occur in practice."
IllegalOverloadAllThermalBattery enter action sets cmd_load_cut_in = 0 and cmd_load_cut_out = 1.
findings.summary: The illegal overload state is reachable under an explicit guard and also sheds load, although the NL describes it as illegal and says it shall never occur in practice.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary metrics: n_transitions_forced = 144, n_transitions_normal = 1.
design_diagnostics_summary reports advisory_count = 179.
Diagnostics include many W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE instances caused by guard-driven external-input classification.
findings.summary: The model has a dense forced-transition classification structure that is acceptable for this NL but produces many advisory diagnostics and may obscure intended mode-to-mode semantics.

evidence: Diagnostic W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for Pbatt_ch_max includes suggested_fix kind delete.
GroundingMap assumptions state Pbatt_dis_max/Pbatt_ch_max were introduced as capacity variables to express battery limits mentioned in the NL.
DSL actions compute Pbatt_charge without using Pbatt_ch_max.
findings.summary: A diagnostic suggested deleting Pbatt_ch_max because it is unused, but deletion would remove a plausible battery-limit input rather than addressing the more likely modeling gap that charge power should be capped.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary metrics: n_states_leaf = 12 and action_count = 12.

GroundingMap source_summary lists assumptions for state names, SoC threshold 0.3, inferred Pd2max/Pbatt limits, and load cut-out behavior.
